newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - SEPT T-BONDS SEEN SEEKING BASE NEAR 112.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - SEPT T-BONDS SEEN SEEKING BASE NEAR 112.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures will likely try to put in a bottom near term after a very sharp downturn this month, technical analysts said.

John Gambino of JBG Technical Analysis said the down move had so far looked like a three-wave countertrend reaction to the April-August advance and a fresh five-wave rally was should follow if last week's low held.

"So long as that low remains intact, the whole down move is an A-B-C reaction," he said. In Elliott Wave theory, the main trends tend to form five-legged sequences, while corrections come in three legs.
September T-bond futures were drifting in the mid-112 area in mid-morning business on Monday. They had fallen to a low of 112-8/32 on Friday from their August 1 high of 116-31/32.
Last week's low coincided with a trendline drawn from the late-April lows and late-May lows, making it a more credible basing level for a renewed uptrend, Gambino added.
"Basis that, I think it's a low-risk entry point (to get long)," he said. "Take out last week's high (115-6/32), and this thing is on its way."
However, he cautioned that a close below the support would open the way to a slide toward the mid-110 area.
Terence Gabriel, technical strategist at I.D.E.A., also anticpated a bounce near term but warned that the downward momentum had yet to dissipate.

"There's a very negative weekly candle pattern, the weekly 'evening star', and the weekly stochastics are breaking down from overbought levels," he said, adding that momentum indicators were also bearish on a daily basis.

Still, he noted that while the downward bias could prevail for some time despite oversold readings on daily oscillators and some other positive indicators, the market should soon start trying to form a basing pattern.
"The other side of the coin is that you have fallen a significant distance and we're now falling to a very important support," he said.
He viewed 111-28/32, a Gann line on the weekly chart, was a good support level backed up by several other support nearby, including the 50-percent retracement of the April-August rally at 111-14/32.
If the market does hold Friday's low today, it would be an inside day, or 'harami' pattern on the candlesticks, which would suggest a pause in the downthrust, he added.

But Gabriel stressed the danger of the smoldering downward bias. He said a break below the 200-day moving average, now at 110-31/32, would turn the longer-term trend more decidedly bearish and send the market down toward 108-31/32.
